_slice: Grande Prairie Public School Division — the education layer
_note: School authorities complete the local picture: the city and county tax bylaws collect an education requisition, and this is where that money lands. Alberta requires every school jurisdiction to file its budget on a standard provincial template, which makes this layer unusually easy to trace — the template itself names the Funding Manual, the enrolment counts, and the prior year's audited statements. Post-secondary was attempted and abandoned this pass; see _dropped.

reports.title: Approved Budget Report
reports.description: Annual budget filed on Alberta Education's standard template for school jurisdiction 3240, covering roughly $117 million of revenue against $118 million of expense for about 8,300 funded students. Discloses its own key assumptions, its enrolment projection, and the reserve limits it is tested against.
reports.cadence_note: School year ending August 31, so its cycle is offset from every municipal and provincial document in the graph by four months.

release_schedule.rule: Approved annual budget report submitted to the Province (Alberta Education) by May 31 each year, ahead of the school year that begins September 1. GPPSD's Division Planning page lists a distinct 'Approved Budget Report' for each school year (2024-2025, 2025-2026, 2026-2027), and the division's most recent budget (for 2026-27, ~$124.5M operating budget) was approved by its board in spring 2026 for the May 31, 2026 provincial submission deadline.
release_schedule.note: Alberta school boards approve their annual budget at a board meeting in May and submit it to Alberta Education by May 31 each year (confirmed via a comparable Alberta board's budget recommendation report stating 'the budget report will be submitted to the Province by May 31'). GPPSD's own board meeting schedule shows regular May meetings (e.g. May 25) consistent with this cycle. The most recent GPPSD budget (2026-27) was already approved before today's date (2026-08-11), so the next occurrence is the 2027-2028 budget, due by May 31, 2027.

reports.title: Audited Financial Statements
reports.description: Annual audited statements to August 31, establishing the accumulated surplus and reserve balances that the following year's budget opens from and is judged against.

entries.covers: Audited Financial Statements for fiscal year ended August 31, 2026

release_schedule.rule: The Board of Trustees approves the Audited Financial Statements annually, prior to submission to Alberta Education by November 30 (fiscal year ends August 31).
release_schedule.note: Province-wide Alberta Education requirement applying to all Alberta school jurisdictions (submission deadline November 30 for the fiscal year ended August 31). GPPSD's own Division Planning page (https://www.gppsd.ab.ca/our-division/division-planning) posts its Audited Financial Statements annually as of August 31 (most recent found: August 31, 2025, at https://www.gppsd.ab.ca/download/541261), consistent with this pattern, but does not itself state the November 30 submission deadline explicitly -- that wording was found on a peer Alberta school division's (Elk Island Public Schools) site, which cites the same Alberta Education requirement that governs GPPSD.

dependencies.basis: The budget template cites the manual by name and is structured around it: 'As per the 2024/25 Funding Manual, a formal request for an exemption to exceed the 2024/25 maximum operating reserve must be approved by the board and submitted to the Minister.' The 6% maximum operating reserve limit the division is tested against, and the grant rates its revenue is built from, both come from the manual — the budget notes ongoing deficits caused by 'rising operational costs ... without corresponding increases in grant rates'.

The Projected Student Statistics schedule reports 8,261 eligible funded students as 'Grade 1 to 12 students eligible for base instruction funding from Alberta Education', counted as at September 30 and reported to the province through PASI, alongside disability counts on the same basis. Nearly all of the division's $113 million of Government of Alberta revenue is these counts multiplied by rates.

reference_period.stated_as: Eligible funded students 'counted as at September 30' and reported to the province through PASI.

dependencies.basis: The accumulated surplus schedule opens from 'Actual balances per AFS at August 31, 2024' of $16,363,413 and carries audited actuals as a comparative column throughout. The budget cannot be built without the prior year's audit closing first.

reference_period.stated_as: Opens from 'Actual balances per AFS at August 31' of the prior year.

dependencies.basis: Alberta school authorities prepare their financial statements under Canadian public sector accounting standards, as both municipalities already in the graph do and as provincial reporting requirements oblige. The GPPSD statements themselves were not read this pass, so the edge rests on the pattern rather than on the document. One PDF away from being documented.

_dropped.why: The post-secondary half of this slice failed, and for a structural reason worth recording. Northwestern Polytechnic publishes its annual report, strategic plan and master academic plan only through Issuu, a third-party page-flipping viewer, with no text-extractable copy on its own domain. The documents exist and are public, but nothing in them can be read or cited the way a municipal PDF can. Municipal reporting turned out to be markedly more machine-readable than post-secondary reporting — a finding about the corpus rather than about the institution.

Both the city and county bylaws levy an 'Opted Out School Board' requisition, and the opted-out board in this region is Grande Prairie & District Catholic Schools. But neither bylaw names it. Identifying the board would be inference from local knowledge, which is exactly what the evidence standard excludes.

_status: SWEPT 2026-08-09 (dropped-sweep, long tail): both _dropped entries read in full. Both correctly reasoned -- Northwestern Polytechnic's Issuu-only publishing is a genuine structural block (no text-extractable copy exists), and the opted-out school board identification is correctly excluded as local-knowledge inference rather than documented fact. No reports or dependencies changed.
